Although the study has adequate sample sizes (6 PPA patients and 8 controls) satisfying I5, it does not provide between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results relevant to a bvFTD versus control comparison (SPM results are reported for PPA vs controls, not bvFTD) — fails I6 and I7. This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=22), meeting sample size requirements. The study used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with voxelwise GLM, TFCE, and reports anatomical clusters with MNI coordinates for bvFTD versus controls and covariate analyses (i.e., between-group contrasts in a defined stereotaxic space). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are presented and described in the text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no excluded comorbidities reported, and not limited to disallowed modalities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and coordinate tables referenced. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included.

Exclusion (E6) applies: the study used a region-of-interest VBM approach restricted to cortical midline structures rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (bvFTD N=22 and controls N=17, both ≥6), I6 (reported between-group voxelwise contrasts with coordinates in MNI space for bvFTD vs controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (paper does not provide at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted to CMS). Therefore the study must be excluded because it reports only ROI-based VBM results with no whole-brain voxelwise findings, violating the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD and Pick's disease cases with adequate overall sample sizes, but the VBM/whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported coordinate/statistical maps are presented for pathologically defined groups (e.g., Pick's, TDP-C, MAPT mutations) rather than for a clinically defined bvFTD group. The paper therefore does not provide a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing a bvFTD clinical group to healthy controls as required. Full text appears complete.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (12 bvFTD at baseline) and controls and uses resting-state fMRI and DTI (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, it reports tract-specific DTI results and ROI/seed-based DMN connectivity analyses rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts reported in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates. Therefore it does NOT meet I6 and I7. This violates exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and E9 (study reports only seed-based FC and DTI methods rather than whole-brain VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the paper must be excluded.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (behavioral variant FTD n=17) and adequate control sample (n=18). However, all voxelwise group-level imaging analyses and reported coordinates are presented for a pooled FTD group (n=52) that combines bvFTD with PPA subtypes; the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast or whole-brain result that isolates the bvFTD subgroup compared directly to controls. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria requiring bvFTD-specific, unpooled whole-brain group results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included), I5 (sample sizes >=6 for patient subgroup and controls), I8 (whole-brain results/coordinates reported in MNI space). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD-only vs controls where bvFTD is not pooled), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from bvFTD-only). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (37 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients), I5 (patient group size ≥6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise regression analyses within the bvFTD sample). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI or Talairach space. Although individual scans were compared to a normative control database to identify hypometabolism, there is no reported group-level bvFTD vs control contrast. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 (no between-group contrast vs controls).

This study uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (probable bvFTD) (I4), and meets the minimum sample-size requirements (18 patients, 50 controls) (I5). However, it does not report between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinate-based whole-brain results; instead it reports network/ROI-based (AAL parcellation) graph-theory metrics and regional labels. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given these points, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires coordinate-based whole-brain voxelwise results.

This empirical study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19), uses voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI (I3), meets sample size requirements (I5), and explicitly reports voxelwise, whole-brain group comparisons (VBM contrast bvFTD vs controls and resting-state connectivity differences) with MNI coordinates (I6, I7). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete) and reports results in acceptable formats (figures and coordinates) (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not only seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and no evidence of excluded comorbid samples). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and uses FDG-PET (meets I3, I4, I5), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses or between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Neuroimaging assessment was visual/rating-based and diagnostic (sensitivity/specificity) rather than voxelwise statistical mapping with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (and by extension I8) are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply directly. Full text appears complete for screening (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (it uses Freesurfer surface-based ROI volumetric analyses), and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD sample included) and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=48, controls n=94). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modalities), I6 (no coordinate-based between-group contrasts reported), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI-based analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet sample-size and group-level whole-brain result requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET was used) and I4 (a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup is present). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (bvFTD patient group n=4, below the required ≥6), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space comparing a bvFTD group to controls — analyses were single-subject SPM comparisons), and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper must be excluded for not satisfying all required inclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=179) meeting sample-size thresholds (I4,I5), and reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates for bvFTD vs controls and interaction effects (I6,I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in text and supplementary materials (I8). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, non-empirical, only DTI/FC/cortical thickness, or samples with disallowed comorbidities) apply. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion in the review focused on bvFTD imaging studies.

This empirical, multi-center study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (probable/possible) and healthy controls, uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (normalized to MNI space) as an imaging modality, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD). Sample sizes meet minimums (bvFTD n=24, controls n=37). The full text contains introduction, methods, voxelwise VBM/TBSS results, and discussion. The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and although it includes DTI, it also includes VBM so E9 does not apply). Full text appears complete.

This paper is a study design/protocol of an ongoing observational cohort (LOF study). It describes planned use of MRI, FDG-PET, and CSF and recruitment of patients with late-onset frontal behavioral change (n=130 so far), but it does not present empirical imaging results. It does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor does it present whole-brain coordinate results. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria (I4, I6, I7) and meets exclusion criterion E8 (non-empirical paper/protocol without original imaging results).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses both voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET (I3). The FTD sample was clinically diagnosed using consensus criteria and explicitly excluded semantic dementia and progressive nonfluent aphasia, indicating the remaining patients represent behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD)/classic FTD (I4). Sample sizes satisfy the minimum (13 FTD patients; 20 controls) (I5). Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise SPM comparisons normalized to standard space (MNI), and report between-group contrasts comparing the FTD group to controls and to AD, with tables/figures of results (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disqualifying comorbidities reported). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical study that performed whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=19; scans available for 16) to healthy controls (n=20). Group-level voxelwise VBM results are reported (tables/figures) with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds, and between-group contrasts and behavioural correlations are described. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required imaging, sample, reporting, and whole-brain criteria are met.

Excluded because imaging modality does not meet I3 (study used Freesurfer volumetric/cortical-thickness analyses, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and patient group size for the relevant MRI analyses is n=5 (<6), violating I5. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 satisfied) but does not provide the required coordinate-based voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space for a bvFTD group (I6/I7 not met). Exclusion criteria met: E9 (study reports cortical thickness/volumetric methods rather than allowed modalities). Therefore the study should be excluded.

Although this is an empirical FDG-PET study with adequate sample sizes and includes behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) participants, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast specifically isolating a bvFTD-only patient group versus controls. The paper reports whole-brain FDG-PET results for an aggregated FTLD group and for anatomically/neuropsychologically defined FTLD subgroups, but bvFTD subjects are pooled within the broader FTLD sample and no bvFTD-specific voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinates for bvFTD vs controls are reported. Therefore it fails to meet the required inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

The study uses VBM, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD, and reports whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with coordinate results for bvFTD vs controls. However, the full text does not specify the number of bvFTD participants in the bvFTD subgroup (the paper references a table with the breakdown but that table is not included in the provided text). Inclusion criterion I5 requires at least 6 participants in the patient subgroup (bvFTD). Because the bvFTD group size cannot be confirmed from the provided full text, I cannot verify I5 and must exclude the study. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met based on available information.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly examines clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients. Imaging modality: voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) is explicitly used. Sample: 22 bvFTD patients and 35 healthy controls (both >6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses with results localized in MNI space and presents between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and vs AD) with coordinate-based results and figures; covariate VBM analyses and overlap maps are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., review article, ROI-only, or disallowed imaging modality) are met. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not report a bvFTD-versus-control whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast in standard coordinate space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=31), I5 (bvFTD and control groups have >=6 participants). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls in MNI/Talairach space—the VBM results are correlational across pooled diagnostic groups, not a direct bvFTD>control voxelwise comparison), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming solely from the bvFTD group). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. It employed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as its imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group analyses. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=16) and healthy controls (n=17), both above the minimum sample sizes. The paper explicitly reports between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and provides results in MNI space (voxel-wise analyses, coordinates and figures/supplementary material referenced). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study (not a review), it reports whole-brain rather than ROI-only results, the sample exclusions for comorbid psychiatric/neurological conditions are described, and it does not rely solely on methods such as seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI/visual-reading analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients included, n=33), I5 (patient group ≥6 and control group ≥6: bvFTD n=33, CN n=22). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise whole-brain contrasts with coordinates in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach); analyses focus on ROI (PCC) SUVr, visual reads, and regression analyses. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded per E6.

This study used VBM and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=20) and reports voxelwise coordinates, but its analyses were restricted to a frontal mask and correlate SEA subscores within the bvFTD group rather than reporting any between-group contrast versus healthy controls. Therefore it does not provide a between-group MNI/Talairach contrast of bvFTD vs controls (I6 not met) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results (analyses were region-restricted to a frontal mask) (I7 not met). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the paper reports region-restricted voxelwise/ROI-style analyses with no whole-brain results. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (patient groups vs controls) with MNI coordinates. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=14), meeting minimum sample size requirements. The paper provides group-level whole-brain VBM results for the bvFTD group compared to controls (tfce FWE-corrected at P<0.005 and coordinate tables/figures), and reports covariate analyses and coordinates in MNI space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, inappropriate modality, or prohibited comorbid samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=23) that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and FDG-PET imaging modalities, with healthy control groups (MRI and PET controls >6). The authors report group comparisons and voxelwise whole-brain SPM results in MNI space (GM and CMRglc comparisons, voxelwise multiple regression correlations with IADL and AQD_iADL), with coordinates and thresholding described. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review; includes whole-brain voxelwise analyses; no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia reported; not limited to ROI-only or excluded modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study reports only ROI/parcellation-based network analyses (AAL 116 parcellation and MST on ROI time series) and does not present group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts in MNI or Talairach space. Exclusion IDs met: E6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (patient n=41, control n=39). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates; results are ROI-/node-level), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result). Therefore the paper does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise reporting and must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because, although it uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with adequate total sample and control sizes (I5), it does not provide a between-group voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). The reported whole-brain VBM results are for FTLD-TDP pathological subtypes (type 1/2/3) rather than a distinct bvFTD diagnostic group, so there is no clear group-level, whole-brain result coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included, n=32) and I5 (patient and control groups >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is Freesurfer-derived regional volumetry from T1 MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in stereotactic space/MNI or Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported), and I8 (no stereotactic coordinates/tables/figures of whole-brain voxelwise results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports regional/ROI analyses using Freesurfer parcellation with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper does not satisfy required imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and whole-brain diffusion tensor imaging (TBSS) to assess grey- and white-matter correlates of disinhibition in clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) patients. The sample includes 14 bvFTD patients and 18 controls (and 15 AD patients). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain VBM analyses aligned to MNI space, with between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD) and tables/figures of results. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported and described in the text and tables. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an empirical VBM study in a clinical bvFTD sample meeting all inclusion criteria: VBM was used (I3); participants included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=27) and age/education-matched controls (n=19) meeting sample size requirements (I4,I5); whole-brain voxelwise between-group VBM contrasts and correlational analyses are reported with MNI coordinates (I6,I7); results are presented in main text/tables and ROI/whole-brain analyses are described (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not resting-state seed-FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only, and no indication of disqualifying comorbidities). The provided full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical multicenter study that uses both resting-state fMRI (functional connectivity/graph-theory) and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) structural analyses. It enrolled clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=52) and healthy controls (N=60), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts using SPM12 with images normalized to MNI space (VBM and fMRI analyses described), and presents whole-brain results (figures, cluster-level statistics, and supporting tables). Results for bvFTD are not pooled with other patient groups for the primary bvFTD vs control contrasts. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=18). Methods describe whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (normalized to template space) and report group-level whole-brain contrasts (controls > FTD) and voxelwise correlations. The bvFTD group is analyzed separately (controls > FTD contrast), satisfying between-group comparisons. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and references; no exclusion criteria (e.g., review, ROI-only, non-empirical, comorbid psychiatric samples, or disallowed modalities) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical VBM study that directly investigates behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=18), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., controls > bvFTD) with coordinates in MNI space and corrected results, and provides correlations between behavioural scores and grey matter volume. This paper meets all inclusion requirements for the review. Imaging modality: voxel‑based morphometry (VBM) is used (I3). The study reports FDG-PET imaging (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4). The bvFTD subgroup that underwent FDG-PET comprised 12 patients (I5: patient group ≥6). This study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has ample patient numbers (I5). Although VBM analyses were performed across a heterogeneous patient sample and ROI analyses were run within bvFTD and svPPA, the paper does not present a whole-brain group-level (bvFTD vs controls) voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This is a clinical/genetic cohort study that does include FDG‑PET in a small subset and includes patients with behavioural-variant FTD, but it does NOT provide the required imaging group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons or coordinate-based between-group contrasts. This full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and resting-state fMRI analyses (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=26) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=22) (I5). This study meets some inclusion criteria: I3 (used voxel-based morphometry), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants, n=20), and I5 (patient and control groups meet minimum sample sizes: bvFTD n=20, controls n=38). This study meets the inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12) (I4); the bvFTD group (n=12) and controls (n=30) meet the ≥6 participant requirement (I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM contrasts for the bvFTD group versus controls using SPM5 with standard MNI normalization (I6,I7); and results are presented in figures and text (I8). This empirical study meets the review objective and satisfies all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4); the neuroimaging sample meets minimum sizes (8 bvFTD patients in imaging analyses, 16 controls; I5); reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts normalized to MNI space (I6) with tables/figures and voxelwise cluster-corrected results (I7); and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/supplementary material (I8). This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and uses VBM, resting-state fMRI, and 18F-FDG PET (I3, I4, I5 satisfied). However, it does not include a healthy/control group comparison and does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing the bvFTD group to controls; instead, analyses extract ROI-based voxelwise measures from NDH-derived network cores and apply SVM classification across patient groups. This full-text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses alongside diffusion MRI, includes a clearly defined clinical bvFTD group (13 bvFTD patients diagnosed by established criteria) and matched healthy controls, and presents group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) VBM/TBSS results in MNI space comparing bvFTD to controls. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study includes FDG-PET and reports on FTD patients (n=36) but does not provide clear whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) to healthy controls in the main text. This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. This is an empirical MRI study that meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) alongside DTI, performs voxel-wise whole-brain SPM analyses in MNI space comparing bvFTD patients to controls (I6, I7), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (13 bvFTD cases) within the sample (I4), and both the patient subgroup and the control group exceed the minimum size of 6 participants (I5). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD versus control contrast are reported and clearly identified (I7, I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=33) and age-matched healthy controls, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts normalized to MNI space. Methods specify VBM preprocessing, two-sample t-tests comparing each disease group (including bvFTD) to controls, with results displayed as statistical maps and supplementary tables. The study thus meets imaging modality (VBM), sample (clinically diagnosed bvFTD), sample size (>6 per group), reporting of between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space, and whole-brain group-level results (figures/tables/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed comorbid samples, not non-empirical, and not limited to DTI/seed-only FC). Full text is present (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study includes bvFTD patients and reports whole-brain VBM results, but it does not present a voxelwise between-group contrast directly comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. It reports VBM comparisons between AD and bvFTD (and behavioral comparisons with controls), but the imaging between-group contrasts required by the review (bvFTD vs healthy controls) are not provided. Therefore not all inclusion criteria are met.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3 met), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (I4 met), and has adequate group sizes (C9ORF72 group n=11; controls n=15) (I5 met). However, the between-group voxelwise contrasts reported are for a genetic subgroup (C9ORF72 mutation carriers) that pools multiple clinical syndromes (bvFTD, FTD–MND, PPA, etc.), not for a bvFTD-only patient group. Therefore the study does not provide a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in standard space (I6 not met) and does not clearly report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributable specifically to a bvFTD-only target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Conclusion: Excluded because it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (results are for a mixed-diagnosis genetic subgroup rather than a bvFTD-only group).

This retrospective case series uses 18F-FDG PET (meets I3) and reports a group of frontotemporal dementia patients (n=7) diagnosed with bvFTD criteria (meets I4) with at least 6 patients in the FTD group (meets I5). However, the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor does it provide whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures required for meta-analysis. There is no healthy control imaging group or BVFTD-vs-control statistical maps/coordinates (fails I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria from the review list (E5–E9) are directly met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including mentions of behavioural-variant FTD) and uses FDG-PET (I3, I4). The FTD patient group is large enough to satisfy sample-size requirements (I5). However, the paper reports only expert visual readings and diagnostic concordance/sensitivity/specificity; it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Excluded on the basis of absence of voxelwise whole-brain results needed for coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=13) with an adequate bvFTD subgroup size (I4, I5) and has full text available, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast that is specific to the bvFTD subgroup versus healthy controls. The study reports SPM comparisons for an aggregated FTD group (mixed FTD spectrum) versus controls and FDG-PET results linked to presence of primitive reflexes across the whole sample, but no bvFTD-only voxelwise results (thus failing I6 and I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results as required.

This is an empirical voxel-wise structural MRI study (longitudinal Jacobian/gray-matter change maps), equivalent to VBM-style analyses, that specifically includes a bvFTD group (n=44) and healthy controls (n=97). Analyses were performed in standardized (MNI) space and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing each FTLD variant (including bvFTD) to controls, with resulting consensus ROI/change maps and effect-size estimates. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6 per group). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study uses VBM (satisfies I3) and has patient groups with n>6 (satisfies I5). However, it does not include participants who were clinically diagnosed with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). There are no reported between-group contrasts comparing a clinically-defined bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons (FTLD-U vs controls; FTLD-MND vs controls) with MNI-based normalization and voxelwise thresholds. Patient group sizes meet the minimum (FTLD-U n=11; FTLD-MND n=7) and the control group (n=18) meets the criterion. All cases fulfilled consensus criteria for frontotemporal dementia and the paper refers to a clinical diagnosis of frontal-variant/frontotemporal dementia, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD for the purposes of this review. The paper provides group-level whole-brain VBM results in text/figures and identifies affected regions. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; modality is VBM). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. Note: the only minor uncertainty is that the manuscript does not repeatedly label subjects explicitly as “bvFTD” in every section, but it states they fulfilled consensus criteria for frontotemporal dementia and discusses frontal-variant cases, so inclusion is justified.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry (I3) with images normalized to MNI space; included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4) and healthy controls (n=21) (I5); reports voxelwise whole-brain VBM results and correlations (FWE-corrected, MNI-normalized) and performs group comparisons/post-hoc tests including bvFTD vs controls (I6, I7). Whole-brain results and supplementary data are referenced and qualifying results appear reported in text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioral-variant cases present (I4) and sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=24; I5). However, the analyses are graph-theory based on a 471-region parcellation and report regional/parcel-wise network metrics rather than voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts. Therefore it does not provide the required between-group, voxelwise whole-brain results (I6 and I7 not met). Because no voxelwise whole-brain coordinate results are reported and analyses are region/parcellation-based only, exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/parcellation analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) applies. Full text appears complete. Exclusion rationale: fails I6 and I7; meets I3,I4,I5; exclusion E6 applies.

This is a protocol/methods paper describing the LEFFTDS cohort and procedures; it does not present empirical, between-group whole-brain imaging results comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease patients to controls. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical/methods-only paper). Inclusion criteria: I3 (uses fMRI acquisition) is satisfied in that the protocol includes intrinsic connectivity (resting-state) fMRI acquisition. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (does not present a sample of clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease patients with diagnostic group data), I5 (no reported group sizes or patient/control counts ≥6), I6 (no reported between-group contrasts in standardized space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis which requires empirical whole-brain comparisons. Full text appears complete (protocol with methods) and not merely an abstract or truncated record.

The study includes FDG-PET imaging and clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with sufficient sample sizes (I3, I4, I5 are satisfied). However, it does not provide any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group contrasts in stereotactic space comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls; analyses reported are single-subject FDG-PET comparisons and correlations rather than group-level voxelwise results. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to be triggered. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses of cerebellar subregions from T1-weighted MRI (atlas-based label fusion), with no voxelwise whole-brain (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET results and no stereotactic coordinates. Exclusion ID met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because key imaging/modality and whole-brain/coordinate requirements are not satisfied, the study cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

Because the meta-analysis requires voxelwise whole-brain imaging results from VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET, and this study provides ROI-based structural volume analyses only, it does not meet the required imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria and must be excluded.

Imaging and sample meet some inclusion criteria: the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=15) (I4) with at least 6 patients and controls present (I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are group-based comparisons of subgroups defined by storytelling characteristics (diagnostically heterogeneous groups) versus healthy controls, not a direct between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast of the bvFTD group versus controls. Therefore the study does not report a bvFTD-specific between-group contrast in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I6) and does not provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample alone (I7). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria met: none (E[]).

Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore EXCLUDED because it does not use the required imaging modalities nor provide voxelwise whole-brain coordinate results; it is ROI-only.

This study uses structural MRI (voxelwise W-score maps/voxel-based morphometry procedures) and has adequate group sizes, but it does NOT meet key review inclusion requirements. Specifically, the sample is familial FTLD mutation carriers pooled across MAPT/GRN/C9orf72 and heterogeneous clinical diagnoses — the paper does not present results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) or Pick’s disease group (I4 not met). The reported analyses summarize voxelwise W-scores within 179 atlas ROIs and use a machine-learning classifier and ROI-integrated weights rather than reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) statistical contrasts with coordinate tables; thus there are no qualifying between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM-type structural MRI methods) and I5 (sample sizes >6). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI/summary-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Therefore the study is excluded for not containing bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates or a dedicated bvFTD patient group.

The study uses FDG-PET (meets I3) but does not explicitly report inclusion of clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease patients (I4 not met). The manuscript reports inclusion of ‘FTLD’ patients but does not specify bvFTD subtype or provide subgroup counts for bvFTD, so it is not possible to confirm the required patient group. The paper does not present any between-group voxel-wise contrasts with coordinates in MNI or Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). Also, the bvFTD/FTLD subgroup sample size is not clearly reported for the whole-brain analyses to verify the ≥6 participants requirement (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with bvFTD among the phenotypes (I4), and has adequate group sizes (30 FTD, 35 controls; I5). However, it does not present a between-group, voxelwise contrast that isolates a bvFTD group compared directly to healthy controls (I6). The reported voxelwise FDG-PET result is a correlation of metabolism with prosocial sexual behavior across a combined patient sample (FTD and CBS), not a whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise result derived from a bvFTD-only vs control contrast (I7). Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 and cannot be included in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and outcome reporting criteria required by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the study reports ROI volumetric analyses using FreeSurfer rather than whole-brain voxelwise results; no VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET voxelwise contrasts are provided). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=26) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is MRI volumetric/ROI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given E6 and failure to satisfy I3/I6/I7, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study that reports group-level voxelwise comparisons for a bvFTD sample. The paper uses VBM (satisfies I3) and includes an ALS-FTD subgroup meeting bvFTD criteria (authors state all ALS-FTD met bvFTD criteria) (satisfies I4). The bvFTD/ALS-FTD group size is 7 and controls n=24, meeting the >=6 participants requirement (I5). The manuscript reports between-group contrasts comparing ALS-FTD (bvFTD) to controls with voxelwise VBM results (significant caudate head cluster, FWE-corrected) and refers to Supplementary Table 2 (implying coordinate reporting), satisfying I6 and I7. Whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and supplementary material (I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and is complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a fronto-temporal dementia (FTD) patient group of n=13 (I5). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of FTD versus controls in Talairach space (I6, I7) and presents results in acceptable forms (I8). However, the paper does not specify that the FTD sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease; diagnostic subtype is not detailed, so inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD or Pick's disease) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I4 (specific diagnosis of bvFTD/Pick's).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=20) and age-matched healthy controls (n=20). Whole-brain voxel-wise VBM analyses (permutation-based GLM) comparing patient groups to controls are reported, with results localised using the Harvard-Oxford atlas and maximum coordinates reported in MNI space. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group (including atrophy patterns and correlations with behavioural measures), satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts specific to bvFTD. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not DTI/FC/cortical-thickness-only; empirical data only). The provided full text contains introduction, methods (including VBM procedures), results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (satisfies I3) and the sample includes some clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (satisfies I4). However, it is excluded because it does not report any between-group contrasts specifically comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met), and it does not present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for a bvFTD-only sample (I7 not met). Additionally, the number of clinically defined bvFTD participants is not reported separately, so the requirement for at least 6 bvFTD patients in the target group cannot be confirmed (I5 not met). The paper analyzes pathologically defined FTLD-TDP subtypes rather than a clinician-diagnosed bvFTD group, so the target sample results required by the review objective are absent. Exclusion criteria: none met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: uses FDG-PET voxelwise analysis (SPM) (I3); participants are clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTLD (fv-FTLD), equivalent to bvFTD in intent (I4); sample sizes meet thresholds (18 patients, 24 controls; MDL subset 8 and 6) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI space comparing fv-FTLD to controls (I6); provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the target fv-FTLD sample (I7); results reported as coordinates and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study uses VBM-like voxel-wise GM/CSF analyses (I3), includes FTD patients with bvFTD among them (I4), and has adequate group sizes (30 FTD, 30 controls; I5), it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast in standard stereotactic space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes. The FTD sample is a mixed group (bvFTD and semantic dementia) and the paper presents individual deviation maps, region-wise ROC/classification results and reader-based comparisons rather than group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts or coordinate tables for a bvFTD vs control comparison. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete.

The study uses VBM-based processing of structural MRI (I3 satisfied) and includes a test FTD group (n=12) and healthy controls (n=18), meeting sample-size requirements (I5 satisfied). However, it does NOT specify that the FTD cases are clinically-diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; FTD is reported without subtyping, so I4 is not met. Crucially, the paper does not report any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast coordinates in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls; results are presented as classifier performance (SVM AUCs, PPV/NPV) and radar plots rather than voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables, so I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused coordinate-based meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the study does not include a healthy/control group nor report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). It is an open-label before/after FDG-PET study with within-subject and subgroup (bvFTD n=7) voxelwise contrasts, but no case–control comparison. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants included), I5 (patient group and bvFTD subgroup ≥6 participants), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for bvFTD subgroup), I8 (results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Because the meta-analysis requires between-group voxelwise contrasts vs controls where bvFTD is not pooled, this paper does not meet I6 and must be excluded.

Although the study used FDG-PET (meets I3) and included an FTD patient group larger than 6 (meets I5), it does not meet key review requirements: the paper does not specify that patients had behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease (I4 not satisfied), and it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing a bvFTD group to controls — no coordinates or voxelwise statistical maps are provided (I6 and I7 not satisfied). Imaging analyses were visual reads and PALZ classifications rather than voxelwise group comparisons. Therefore it must be excluded under E6 (no whole-brain results reported).

This paper reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses comparing MSTD mutation carriers (early-stage bvFTD cases) to age- and gender-matched controls. Methods explicitly describe optimized and modulated VBM (SPM2) and report statistically significant voxelwise grey matter loss (P<0.05 FDR-corrected) with stereotactic locations referenced in supplementary Table 4. The sample used for VBM comprised 7 MSTD patients (bvFTD; early-stage) and 19 controls, satisfying minimum group sizes. The results are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) and coordinate/stereotactic localization is provided (in supplemental). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, contains whole-brain voxelwise results, not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; supplementary coordinate table is referenced. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; N=74) and I5 (patient group >=6). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (study does not use Voxel-Based Morphometry, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET — it uses visual rating of conventional structural MRI), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast reported in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy required imaging modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria and must be excluded from the review.

The study uses VBM and includes a bvFTD subgroup (I3, I4) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=11; controls n=39) (I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlations within the combined FTLD patient cohort and results are reported using pre-specified small-volume (ROI) correction; the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group separately to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (a between-group contrast for bvFTD vs controls and at least one whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from the bvFTD group) are not met. In addition, the reported significant imaging finding derives from ROI/small-volume analysis rather than whole-brain voxelwise results, fitting exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The paper reports between-group, whole-brain VBM contrasts for PiD versus controls (voxelwise results derived from MNI-normalized data) and presents regional atrophy findings in figures and tables, satisfying I6, I7, and I8.
