Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion based on the PiD group whole-brain VBM results relevant to the review objective.

Although this empirical study includes VBM (I3), enrolled clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=7) (I4), and has an adequately sized control group (HC n=21) with the bvFTD group ≥6 participants (I5), it does NOT report a between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The VBM results reported are correlation/conjunction analyses across the pooled participant sample and semantic/eating-behavior covariates, rather than a group-level bvFTD vs. control whole-brain voxelwise contrast attributable solely to the bvFTD group (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

EXCLUDED: This study used T1-weighted structural MRI with multi-atlas ROI volumetry focused on frontal regions, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET (I3 not met). It reports region-based volumes and regression/ANOVA results but no whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=18), I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports original empirical voxel-wise resting-state fMRI and VBM analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD (n=25) and AD (n=31) patients and healthy controls (n=29). Imaging and analysis were registered to MNI-152 space and voxel-wise, whole-brain group contrasts (TFCE, FWE-corrected, permutation testing) are reported for bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD (network-to-region and region-to-region voxelwise results). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). The paper provides methods, results, and discussion (complete full text). Thus all required inclusion criteria for the review are met (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria required for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I5 (patient group sizes: FTLD N=31, AD N=42). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Pick’s disease — participants are described as FTLD without specification of bvFTD/Pick’s subgroup), I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the paper does not provide whole-brain between-group results for the target diagnosis; analyses rely on ROI-based logistic regression and within-subject correlations rather than group-level whole-brain contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the article does not provide the required bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinate-based between-group results and must be excluded.

Excluded because the study reports lobar/ROI volumetry and group comparisons but does not present whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or coordinate tables in a defined stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based volumetry via SPM5, comparable to VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTLD patients), I5 (sample sizes: 6 bvFTLD patients and 30 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts with MNI/Talairach coordinates comparing bvFTLD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results clearly identified as from the bvFTLD group). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present). Therefore the paper does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain coordinate-based inclusion.

This study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports voxelwise group contrasts with anatomical coordinates in MNI space. Participant samples include clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (C9 mutation carriers, n=8; sporadic bvFTD, n=15) and healthy controls (n=15), meeting minimum group sizes. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results comparing bvFTD groups to controls and reports neural correlates of episodic memory for the target bvFTD subgroups (MNI coordinates referenced; figures and supplementary table cited). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The paper uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=18) and controls (n=28) meeting the sample size threshold (I4, I5). It also reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise covariate results identified for the bvFTD sample (e.g., modified net score correlations) so I7 is satisfied. However, the provided full text does not present any explicit between-group voxelwise contrast results (bvFTD vs. controls) reported in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) as required by I6. Although group comparisons are mentioned in methods, no between-group coordinate results or contrast maps for bvFTD versus controls are given in the excerpt. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to apply. Therefore the study is excluded because inclusion criterion I6 is not met.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of 70 frontal-variant FTD (fv-FTD) patients that reports voxelwise, group-level PCA maps (whole-brain metabolic covariance) and clinical correlations. It meets imaging modality (I3), clinically diagnosed frontal/bvFTD sample (I4), adequate patient sample size (I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results derived from the patient group (I7). However, the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) directly comparing the bvFTD/fv-FTD group to healthy controls (no coordinate-based bvFTD vs control contrast presented), so it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Hence the study is excluded for not meeting I6.

The study uses VBM and resting-state fMRI (satisfies I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the patient sample (satisfies I4), and has adequate group sizes (14 patients, 16 controls; satisfies I5). However, the reported voxelwise whole-brain contrasts are presented for the combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixed bvFTD and avPPA) versus controls. The manuscript does not report a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls, nor whole-brain results that are explicitly and exclusively from a bvFTD subgroup. Therefore it fails I6 (no bvFTD-specific between-group contrast) and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6/I7 are not met, the study must be excluded.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and inclusion criteria: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality, includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=26) satisfying sample-size thresholds, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM analyses. The manuscript states that VBM group comparisons (each patient group vs. healthy controls) and their results are reported (in Supplementary Information S11), and the main text reports multiple voxelwise, FWE-corrected VBM results in MNI space and TBSS/DTI whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, includes VBM whole-brain results, excludes comorbid psychiatric/substance cases in recruitment). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary group-contrast results are referenced (acceptable per I8). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

This study includes FTD and uses FDG-PET (meets I3) but does not meet other key inclusion criteria. The FTD cohort is not specified as behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease; the paper refers broadly to FTD and mixed clinical syndromes (I4 not met). The methods and results present ROI-based PET/MRI biomarkers, derived indices (API-PET, occipital vs. temporal index) and classifier performance, but do not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level between-group contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls; no voxel-coordinate tables or explicit whole-brain voxelwise results are provided in the main text (I6 and I7 not met). Sample details for the FTD subgroup size are not clearly reported here to confirm ≥6 patients (I5 not confirmed/not met). Therefore the study effectively reports ROI/derived-index analyses only and lacks qualifying whole-brain voxelwise evidence (meets exclusion E6). Full text appears complete.

The study uses VBM (I3) and includes >=6 patients and >=6 controls overall (I5). However, it does not clearly report clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease specifically—participants are listed as ‘FTD’ without specifying bvFTD (I4 not met). The paper does not present any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). Although whole-brain VBM correlations are reported across a mixed diagnostic sample, there are no group-level whole-brain results specific to a bvFTD group (I7 not met). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group used as a reference) and I5 (bvFTD group n=9 and controls n=17, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, task or resting-state fMRI, or FDG‑PET — methods were ASL, DTI and atlas-based GM %ICV measures), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported for the bvFTD sample). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (the paper lacks voxelwise whole-brain results; reported summary/global and lobar measures rather than coordinate-based, voxelwise contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients with behavioral features consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD/Pick’s-type presentation) (I4). The imaging analyses include at least 6 patients in the target patient group (6 overeating FTD patients) and 47 controls, satisfying minimum sample size requirements (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing the overeating FTD group (a bvFTD subgroup) to controls and to nonovereating patients, with coordinates provided (I6). Whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results (reported within an a priori ROI but using voxelwise statistics and correction) are presented as group-level findings clearly attributed to the target sample (I7), and results/coordinates are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) with supplementary material noted but not required.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses FDG-PET imaging; (I4) includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (both probable and pathologically confirmed definite cases); (I5) sample sizes exceed the minimum (multiple bvFTD groups and healthy control groups with n>>6 at each site); (I6) reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise results in MNI space (scans reoriented to MNI space and a bvFTD-related spatial covariance topography [bFDRP] identified that discriminates patients from controls); (I7) provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise topographies clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample (thresholded voxel maps, bootstrap reliability, and voxelwise correlation analyses reported); (I8) results are presented as figures/maps and clearly described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review/meta-analysis; not ROI-only; empirical data; not solely seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness; no disqualifying comorbid sample described). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

Although this study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically defined FTLD group diagnosed using Neary criteria consistent with behavioral variant features (I4) with n=11 patients (I5), it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). PET results are presented as regional hypometabolism summaries/ROI z-scores and categorical ROI counts rather than voxelwise coordinates or whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 and reports only ROI-based analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses (FSL VBM) with voxel-wise GLM and permutation testing; includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=13) and healthy controls (n=12); sample sizes exceed minimums; between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported with MNI coordinates and figures; group-level whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1 MRI (I3). It includes an ALS-FTD subgroup (n=18) meeting Neary criteria for FTD with prominent behavioral abnormalities, consistent with clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4). Patient (n=18) and control (n=15) group sizes exceed the minimum of 6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of the ALS-FTD group versus neurologic controls in MNI space (tables/figures with coordinates are referenced), satisfying between-group coordinate reporting and whole-brain evidence (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Supplementary tables/coordinates are referenced but their absence does not prevent verification of reported whole-brain VBM results.

The study uses FDG-PET with whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (I3 met). However, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to controls. The FTLD group is heterogeneous (FTD, SD, mixed) and the explicit FTD/bvFTD subgroup size is only N=3 (below the required N≥6), and the reported group comparisons are for FTLD as a whole versus SCI, not for bvFTD unpooled. Therefore criteria I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 bvFTD patients), I6 (between-group contrast for bvFTD vs controls), and I7 (group-level whole-brain result clearly from target bvFTD sample) are not met. Full text appears complete. Hence the study is excluded for not meeting the bvFTD-specific inclusion criteria.

Although the paper uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes a substantive FTD patient subgroup (47 FTD patients, likely bvFTD; I4), and meets sample-size requirements (I5), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts specifically comparing a bvFTD (FTD) group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The neuroimaging results are voxelwise brain–behavior correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample rather than group-level bvFTD vs. control whole-brain contrasts, and thus do not provide a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Hence excluded for failing I6 and I7.

Although this is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), uses FDG‑PET as an imaging modality (I3), and meets the minimum sample-size requirement for patients and controls in the discovery sample (I5: bvFTD n=18, controls n=29), it does not report any between‑group whole‑brain (voxelwise) contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The 18F‑FDG PET analyses reported are voxelwise regressions of metabolic signal against oculomotor parameters performed in a subset of patients (18 patients: 6 AD, 7 bvFTD, 5 svPPA) and no PET data from controls are reported. Thus the paper fails to meet I6 (between‑group bvFTD vs. controls contrast) and I7 (a group‑level whole‑brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an original empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients presenting the behavioral syndrome (bvFTD phenotype): 9 FTD patients (after excluding PA/SD and other outliers) and 26 healthy controls. Imaging modality is VBM (SPM99) on whole-brain T1 MRI. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain contrasts (SPM voxel-by-voxel comparisons) with stereotactic coordinates (e.g., periaqueductal gray center at (0, -28, -10)) and corrected P-values; small-volume correction was also used. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are triggered; the study is empirical, not ROI-only, does not rely solely on other modalities, and does not appear to include excluded comorbid samples. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis targeting bvFTD VBM studies.

Exclusion reason: The study reports only ROI/parcellation-based functional connectivity and graph-theory edge/node metrics, not whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) contrasts. It does not report a between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls; subgroup analyses compare bvFTD+/ALS-FTD to ALS-only, and the main comparison pools all C9+ carriers vs controls. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD present among participants), I5 (patient subgroup and control group sizes meet the minimum: bvFTD+ symptomatic n=9, controls n=26). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD group vs controls where bvFTD group is not pooled), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported from the target bvFTD sample). Full text appears complete. Hence EXCLUDED.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain group-level contrasts relating cortical atrophy in a bvFTLD (bvFTD) subgroup to controls, with coordinates in MNI space. The bvFTLD patient group is sufficiently large (bvFTLD n=71 overall; imaging subset n=51) and compared to an age-matched control cohort (n≈42–43). Results for the bvFTLD group are reported separately (not pooled) and include whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinate tables. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=31) and healthy controls (n=56) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group, and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls and bvFTD ε4-carrier analyses) analyzed in standard space using SPM5 with results presented in figures and Supplementary Table S2. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and describes voxelwise whole-brain analyses and contrasts specific to the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This empirical study includes task-based BOLD fMRI and voxel-based morphometry-style volumetric analyses relating gray matter density to behavior, and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient sample. Imaging modality (task fMRI and voxelwise gray-matter analysis) meets I3. The sample comprises 16 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with MRI data available for a subset (N=11) and healthy controls (N=14) for the imaging analyses; both patient and control imaging groups exceed N=6 (I5). The paper reports between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (two-sample t-tests in SPM8) comparing bvFTD to healthy seniors with FDR-corrected results and reported regions/figures/tables in stereotactic space (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not exclusively other modalities, and comorbid causes were excluded). Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

Excluded because the imaging modality used is deformation-based morphometry (DBM), which is not one of the eligible modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — inclusion criterion I3 is not met. The paper does not provide group-level results in a standard stereotaxic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables, so I6 is not met. In addition, the sample includes 5 FTD subjects who also meet criteria for possible/probable ALS (a concurrent neurological condition), triggering exclusion criterion E7. The study does meet I4 (clinically-diagnosed FTD consistent with behavioral variant description), I5 (N=22 patients and N=22 controls), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures). Full text appears complete.

This is a VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral variant) subgroup (n=30) and healthy controls (n=20) and reports whole-brain voxelwise findings. However, the paper does not present a between-group whole-brain contrast comparing the bvFTD (FTD variant) group directly to healthy controls in stereotactic coordinates. The authors explicitly excluded normal controls from VBM analyses and instead report correlational VBM results across the mixed patient sample and subgroup interactions within patients (FTD vs non-FTD). Therefore Inclusion criterion I6 (direct between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls in defined stereotactic space) is not met, so the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI (I3) and includes seven FTD patients (I5). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates transformed to Talairach and provides tables/supplementary material (I7, I8). However, it does not present a between-group contrast of the FTD (bvFTD) group versus healthy controls in a standard space; the between-group comparisons are FTD versus AD, not versus controls, so inclusion criterion I6 is not met. Additionally, the paper does not explicitly state that the FTD sample is the behavioral variant (bvFTD) as required by I4 (diagnosis was by Lund-Manchester criteria but variant not specified), so I4 is uncertain/not clearly satisfied. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria (notably I6) and is excluded. No exclusion criteria from the list are met.

The study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) and reports group-level voxelwise results (Talairach normalization) for an FTD group (I7, I8). Sample sizes meet minimums (FTD n=29, controls n=12; I5). However, it does not report results specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as a separate group (I4 not met). The FTD sample includes mixed subtypes (15 primary progressive aphasia, 14 with social/executive disorder) and analyses/contrasts are presented for the combined FTD group rather than a standalone bvFTD subgroup; therefore no between-group contrast in stereotactic space comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls is available (I6 not met). Because key inclusion criteria I4 and I6 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

The study uses structural T1 MRI with voxelwise gray-matter probability maps (VBM-style) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=41) and controls (n=56), meeting I3, I4, and I5. However, the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD versus controls in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach). Instead, it reports multivariate SCCAN associations across a mixed cohort and presents network-level correlations, not group-level bvFTD>control whole-brain contrasts. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and cannot be included.

This study meets several inclusion criteria relevant to the review: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients (10 bvFTD participants) (I4), has sufficient sample sizes in patient and control groups (bvFTD n=10, controls n=20) (I5), and reports whole-brain VBM results/figures (I8). However, it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast (in MNI or Talairach space) that compares the bvFTD group separately to healthy controls (i.e., bvFTD not pooled with other FTLD subgroups), which is required by I6. In addition, although whole-brain VBM correlational analyses are reported for the combined FTLD group and subgroup correlates are mentioned, the paper does not clearly present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result that is explicitly and clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone (I7). No exclusion criteria from E5–E9 are triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded for failing inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

Exclusion decision: No between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD / SOC/EXEC) patients to healthy controls was reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM was used), I4 (the sample includes a SOC/EXEC subgroup corresponding to bvFTD), I5 (sample sizes: 64 patients, 13 healthy controls overall; imaging subset included 17 patients), I7 (the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results—voxel-based morphometry correlations within the patient group). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the study did not report at least one between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls; imaging analyses were within-group correlations and did not include an explicit voxelwise patient vs. control comparison). Exclusion criteria met: none (not a review; not ROI-only; not excluded modalities). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically defined FTD group meeting Neary criteria (described with behavioral symptoms consistent with bvFTD; I4) with n=11 and controls n=17 (I5). However, the VBM analysis is a covariate/regression across all subjects (patients collapsed with controls) and reports correlations between performance and gray matter volume rather than reporting a between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to controls in stereotactic space. Therefore it does not meet I6 (no between-group bvFTD vs control contrast) nor I7 (no group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered.

This study does not meet key imaging and reporting criteria for the review. Although it includes a sufficient patient sample (29 FTD patients; meets I5), the imaging methods reported are SPECT and PET without specification that PET is FDG-PET and do not include VBM or fMRI (I3 not met). Importantly, the study does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or provide coordinates from between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). The sample is described as early FTD but not explicitly as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). The neuroimaging analyses relied on visual inspection and quadrant categorization rather than voxelwise coordinate-based reporting, so it fails the requirement for whole-brain results; this places it under exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain results). Therefore exclude.

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including frontal-variant cases), uses voxel-based morphometry, has adequate sample sizes (18 patients, 17 controls), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise results. However, the patient group is heterogeneous (SD, fvFTD and mixed cases) and the paper does not present a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD/fvFTD-only group to controls without pooling with other FTD subtypes. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no bvFTD-only between-group voxelwise contrast). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met.

This is an empirical MRI volumetric ROI study of 21 FTD patients comparing subcortical VOIs by apathy status. It does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3), does not specify clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (fails I4), and reports only region-of-interest volumetric comparisons with no whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (fails I6 and I7). It meets the sample size criterion (I5: 21 patients). It therefore meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM and reports whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts comparing ALS/FTLD to controls, with sufficient sample sizes and includes patients meeting frontal-variant FTLD criteria (bvFTD-like). However, the provided full text does not explicitly report between-group results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach) or provide coordinate tables/coordinates for the bvFTD/FTLD patient contrasts. Inclusion criterion I6 (reporting at least one between-group contrast in a defined stochastic space) is not satisfied based on the available text, so the study cannot be included for a coordinate-based meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast that clearly compares a bvFTD (behavioral-variant) subgroup to controls without pooling with other FTD subtypes. Specifically, inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD vs. controls contrast not pooled) and I7 (whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD subgroup) are not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients—48/62 characterized as behavioral presentation), I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls), and I8 (results reported in tables/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study of eight clinically diagnosed FTD patients (meets I3: FDG-PET modality, and I5: patient group n=8). However, the paper does not clearly report that the sample is specifically behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not clearly met). Crucially, no between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls are reported; results are descriptive/individual patient PET patterns and correlations with neuropsychology rather than group-level voxelwise coordinate tables or statistical maps (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it falls under exclusion E6 (no whole-brain results / likely ROI/visual analyses only). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

This study is excluded. Exclusion criterion met: E6 — the study uses SPECT quadrant/region ratings (visual ratings) and does not report whole-brain, voxelwise results (only regional/ROI-style ratings). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD patients with behavioural presentation; PPA/semantic dementia excluded), I5 (sample size: 74 FTD patients). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is SPECT, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study does not meet the imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria required by the meta-analysis. Although sample sizes are sufficient (I5 satisfied), the imaging modality was structural T1 volumetry/ROI analyses (frontotemporal volumes derived from an atlas-based SPM8 pipeline), not Voxel-Based Morphometry, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls, nor does it provide stereotactic coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Also, the sample comprises autosomal-dominant FTLD mutation carriers (mixed clinical syndromes) rather than explicitly clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease (I4 not met). Therefore E6 applies (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses VBM as one of the imaging methods, it does NOT report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for the bvFTD group. The paper reports classification performance (sensitivity) using automated MRI quantification and DSI but does not present group-level voxelwise results or coordinate tables/figures that identify whole-brain results from the target bvFTD sample. This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study (SPM/DARTEL in MNI space) comparing genetic FTLD groups to healthy controls. The MAPT mutation group consisted entirely of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and is analysed separately from other patient groups, providing between-group voxelwise contrasts versus controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds (MAPT n=11, GRN n=9, controls n=15). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported (cross-sectional VBM and longitudinal VCM analyses) and presented in standard stereotactic space. The study is not a review, not ROI-only, and does not use excluded modalities only. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) in SPM99 to perform whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing the SOC/EXEC patient subgroup (n=12) to 12 healthy controls and reported significant clusters (right orbital frontal, superior temporal, visual association, posterior cingulate). The SOC/EXEC subgroup corresponds clinically to the behavioral/social-executive presentation of FTD (behavioral variant). Sample sizes meet the ≥6 requirement for patients and controls. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results derived from the target patient subgroup (clusters/BA with p-values and figure), satisfying whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and no disqualifying comorbidities reported). Confidence is moderate because the subgroup is labeled SOC/EXEC rather than explicitly “bvFTD” in the excerpt and explicit MNI/Talairach coordinates are not displayed in the provided text, though SPM normalization and voxelwise results were used and cluster locations were reported.

Full text is complete. Meets I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among sample), I5 (patient and control groups each >=6), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). However it does NOT meet I6 and I7: the reported between-group VBM results are for genetic subgroups (PGRN+ vs PGRN−) that include mixed clinical phenotypes (bvFTD, SD, CBS) rather than a bvFTD-only group, and no between-group contrast is reported specifically for a bvFTD-only sample in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinate tables. Direct comparisons are genetic-group level, not bvFTD-only voxelwise contrasts, so the study cannot be included for a meta-analysis targeting bvFTD-specific whole-brain coordinates. No exclusion criteria from E5–E9 were triggered.

The full text reports a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study (SPM99) with whole-brain, voxelwise results reported in Talairach space. The sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patients with a clearly defined non-aphasic subgroup (NON-APH; described as social/behavioral impairment consistent with behavioral variant presentation) of n=14, meeting the bvFTD group requirement. Imaging control group (n=12) meets control size criterion. The paper provides subgroup vs healthy-senior VBM contrasts and tables/figures of coordinates (Tables 3–5, Fig.2) showing whole-brain results for FTD subgroups versus controls, not pooled with other patient groups. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; no proscribed comorbid sample or disallowed modalities). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore study meets all inclusion criteria for this review.

This study is excluded because the patient group is reported as heterogeneous FTLD without specification of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease (I4 not met). While the study meets imaging and analysis requirements (uses FDG-PET and voxel-wise whole-brain analyses; I3, I7, and I8 are satisfied), it does not report a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls (I6 not met). Additionally, the paper does not provide explicit counts confirming at least 6 bvFTD patients and 6 controls for the target comparison (I5 not met / cannot be confirmed). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it uses surface-based morphometry measures (cortical thickness and fractal dimension) rather than the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) — meeting exclusion criterion E9. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included; 8 bvFTD cases reported) and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=8, controls n=28 >6). The paper also reports group-level whole-brain vertex-wise results identified for bvFTD (I7). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is SBM/cortical thickness/fractal dimension, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET) and I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in a defined stereotactic space such as MNI/Talairach with coordinates). Because I3 is not met and the study falls under E9, it does not qualify for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s bvFTD imaging inclusion criteria. The paper reports a sample of mild Alzheimer’s disease (AD) subjects (not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease), uses FreeSurfer ROI volumetry (structural ROI volumes) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and presents ROI-based associations rather than whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the analyses are ROI-based with no voxelwise, coordinate-based whole-brain results in standardized space. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality), I4 (bvFTD sample), I6 (between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result for target group).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the imaging modality used is 99mTc-ECD SPECT, not VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant/bvFTD patients as fvFTD subgroup), I5 (patient group N=48 and control group N=15, both ≥6), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with reported coordinates comparing clinical subgroups to controls), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality mismatch). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it used VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) (I4), had sufficient sample sizes for patient and MRI control groups (I5), and reported between-group contrasts/comparisons involving the bvFTD group with coordinate-based results (I6). However, the paper does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample alone; the whole-brain VBM result reported is for the combined FTD group, while bvFTD-specific findings are reported using ROI/SVC analyses. Therefore it effectively reports only ROI-restricted/via small-volume-corrected results for bvFTD, triggering exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results for the target group). Inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain evidence for the target group) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This VBM study included 16 FTLD patients (13 clinically characterized as FTD with early prominent behavioural features) and 9 healthy controls and reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM results and coordinates for group comparisons and behavioural covariates. However, the critical requirement for the meta-analysis is that between-group contrasts be reported specifically for a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group compared to controls (i.e., bvFTD group not pooled with other patient subtypes). In this paper the patient group is analysed as FTLD (mixed: FTD + SD) for the between-group comparison, and no separate group-level whole-brain contrast is reported that isolates only bvFTD patients versus controls. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients), I5 (sample sizes ≥6), I8 (results/coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Because it does not provide a bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group contrast, the study is excluded.

Study includes clinically diagnosed behavioral/frontal variant FTD patients (n=142) and uses FDG-PET imaging with voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses reporting coordinates in Talairach space. Patient and control group sizes exceed the minimum (patients n=142; PET subgroup patients n=41, controls n=16). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain between-group contrasts (patients vs. controls and H1 vs H2 carriers) with voxelwise results and coordinates, and results are clearly attributable to the behavioral variant FTD sample (not pooled with other patient groups). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) and healthy controls (n=20). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise VBM analyses in MNI space: separate patient-group atrophy contrasts (bvFTD vs Controls and AD vs Controls) and covariate whole-brain analyses correlating future-thinking performance with gray matter, with results corrected and presented in tables/figures and described in the text. Sample sizes meet the threshold (bvFTD n>=6; controls n>=6). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not an excluded modality, and clinical exclusions for comorbidity were applied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses FDG-PET and SPM voxelwise whole-brain analysis and includes a clinical FTLD sample (FTD n=9, total FTLD n=14), with MNI/Talairach coordinates reported. However, the paper reports results for a combined FTLD group (FTD, semantic dementia, PPA) compared to early-onset AD; it does not present whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts specific to behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) alone. Therefore it fails the requirement that bvFTD not be pooled with other patient groups in the reported contrasts (I6) and fails to provide whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample (I7). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a sufficient FTD patient group (14 FTD cases) meeting the sample size requirement (I5) and contains Pick's disease cases (I4). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to controls with reported coordinates. The analyses and results are presented as diagnostic assessments, regional summaries and individual SSP statistical maps, but no whole-brain group-level voxelwise coordinates or tables are provided; therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This corresponds to exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia group using Neary criteria (I4) with N=17 (I5 satisfied). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the (behavioral) FTD group to healthy controls; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables are presented (I6 and I7 not met). The FTD subgroup is reported but not explicitly labelled as behavioral-variant (bvFTD), and analyses are presented as individual/clinical reads and diagnostic accuracy statistics rather than voxelwise group results. Therefore the paper fails to meet mandatory inclusion criteria I6 and I7 and is excluded.

This is a case-report/series of two p.A53T SNCA mutation carriers presenting with FTD-like phenotype. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants clinically diagnosed with bvFTD/FTD features). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — only structural MRI visual assessment and DaTSCAN), I5 (patient group size <6), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria from the review (E5–E9) are clearly triggered. Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods/cases, results, discussion). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails multiple required inclusion criteria (imaging modality and sample size and whole-brain voxelwise reporting).

This is an MRI volumetry/visual-rating study of hippocampal atrophy in FTLD and AD, not a VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET study (I3 not met). The imaging approach is ROI-based (hippocampal volumetry and MTA visual ratings) and the paper does not report whole‑brain, voxelwise results in a standard stereotactic space (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole‑brain results) applies. The sample size criterion is satisfied (FTLD n=42, controls n=73) so I5 is met. The paper reports FTD as a subgroup, but does not explicitly state “behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD)” or Pick’s disease, so I4 is uncertain/not clearly met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because imaging modality and analysis do not meet VBM/fMRI/FDG‑PET and whole‑brain voxelwise reporting requirements (E6).

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results and has adequate patient numbers, but it does not include or report results specifically for clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. The FTLD group is pathologically defined and subdivided by molecular pathology (FTLD-Tau, FTLD-TDP43), and some clinical syndromes (e.g., semantic dementia) are discussed, but no bvFTD (or Pick’s) group-level contrast versus controls in standard stereotactic space is presented. Therefore I4 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is an empirical VBM study with adequate sample sizes (FTD n=8; controls n=26) and reports voxelwise coordinates, but it does not clearly study behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) specifically. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6), and I8 (reports voxel coordinate results). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as FTD without specification that they are clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no reported between-group contrast in defined stereotaxic space comparing a bvFTD group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Because the target sample (bvFTD) is not clearly represented, the study must be excluded for not meeting key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7.

Excluded because key inclusion criteria were not all met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used voxel-wise MRI analyses and FDG-PET), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I7 (reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing patients to controls), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/STAND-maps). This study used structural MRI volumetric and cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Results are reported as regional volumes/thicknesses (ROIs) rather than voxelwise whole-brain coordinates in MNI/Talairach space. The FTD group (n=22) is not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring an eligible imaging modality (I3), a target patient sample (bvFTD/Pick’s; I4), and voxelwise whole-brain results/coordinates (I6/I7). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses / no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (reports cortical thickness/volumetry methods rather than acceptable modalities). No inclusion criteria are fully satisfied for the review. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (including figures) for patient groups vs controls, and has adequate group sizes; however it does NOT include a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease group nor report a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group (unpooled) to controls. The patient imaging contrasts are for ALS-FTD, ALS, and SD groups; the ALS-FTD group includes patients with FTD+ALS but is not a pure bvFTD sample as required by the review criteria, and the inclusion criterion I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s disease-sample requirements and must be excluded.

The study used FDG-PET and reports whole-brain SPM voxelwise comparisons with sufficient sample sizes (FTD n=7; controls n=18). However, the patient group is described generally as 'FTD' without specification of behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease, so it does not meet the key population requirement (I4). Therefore it cannot be included in a bvFTD-focused meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's), I6 (between-group contrasts specifically for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (whole-brain results from a confirmed bvFTD target group), I8 (format applicability for bvFTD-specific results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts in Montreal Neurologic Institute space relating frontal/temporal atrophy to behavioral symptoms. The sample includes 40 clinically diagnosed FTLD patients with a SOC/EXEC subgroup (n=26) corresponding to behavioral-variant presentations, and MRI analyses on 32 patients vs 27 healthy controls (all >6). The paper reports subgroup contrasts (e.g., apathetic and disinhibited subgroups vs controls) and masked whole-brain regression analyses with explicit statistical thresholds, meeting the review’s requirements for imaging modality, target clinical population, minimum sample sizes, and whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core data are presented (tables/figures referenced), so fulltext is sufficient for screening.

This study is excluded because it does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain between-group contrasts specifically comparing the bvFTD group to controls (i.e., no bvFTD-vs-control MNI/Talairach group-level contrast reported). (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD participants included; n=58), I5 (bvFTD and control groups both >6 participants). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls in stereotactic space; analyses are across a pooled NDG sample and correlational VBM with behavioral measures), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from bvFTD group alone). Full text appears complete. No other exclusion criteria were triggered.

This multicenter empirical study included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (44) and healthy controls (60) and used both resting-state fMRI connectivity and voxel-based morphometry (VBM)/structural MRI analyses. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (whole-brain voxelwise analysis described) and presents anatomical distribution of significant effects, fulfilling whole-brain result requirements; the methods follow standard VBM/voxelwise pipelines consistent with MNI-space reporting (I6,I7). Resting-state fMRI FC and VBM are explicitly used (I3) and results/figures/tables are described in the main text (I8). Patients were clinically diagnosed as probable bvFTD per consensus criteria (I4). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study should be excluded. Exclusion basis: E6 (study reports only ROI-based regional gray matter volumes with no whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (sample size: 18 FTLD patients and 14 controls) and I4 (sample includes clinical FTD cases, i.e., frontotemporal dementia subtype). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI region-based volumetry, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in stereotactic space comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls; patients were analyzed as a pooled FTLD group), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper does not provide the whole-brain, stereotactically-localized contrasts required for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain analysis requirements for the review. It reports structural MRI visual and regional atrophy descriptions, not Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM), fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not present whole-brain voxelwise results in standardized (MNI/Talairach) space or coordinate tables/figures for a bvFTD group vs controls (I6, I7 not met). The sample is a heterogeneous set of PGRN mutation carriers with varied clinical diagnoses (FTD, PPA, CBS, parkinsonism, AD-like presentations) but does not define or analyze a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group separately (I4 not met). Although multiple affected individuals and MRI scans are reported, there is no clear bvFTD patient group with >=6 subjects and no voxelwise between-group contrast against controls (I5 not met). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the review checklist are directly triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []).

This study uses VBM (I3 met), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 met), and has sufficient sample sizes (47 bvFTD patients, 34 controls) (I5 met). However, it does NOT report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space where the bvFTD group is analyzed separately (I6 not met). Although whole-brain VBM analyses are reported, they are correlational analyses across the combined FTD patient sample (associating atrophy with happiness behavior) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically for bvFTD vs controls (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

Exclusion E6 met: the study uses ROI/atlas-based regional (AAL) FDG-PET parcellation and metabolic connectivity analyses rather than reporting whole-brain voxelwise (MNI/Talairach) group-level contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTLD patients — 35 behavioral-variant cases), I5 (patient and control group sizes exceed 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group, voxelwise coordinate-based contrast comparing bvFTD separately to controls — FTLD variants were pooled), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results clearly reported for the target bvFTD sample). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis, despite containing relevant FDG-PET data and bvFTD participants, because it lacks the required whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results and reports only ROI/parcellation-based connectivity findings.

This is an empirical study of 72 FTD patients using SPECT and MRI visual ratings. It does not use the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Although the sample size criterion (I5) is met (72 patients), the study fails key inclusion criteria: I3 (imaging modality), I6 (stereotactic between-group contrasts), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results). I4 (explicit inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is not clearly satisfied because participants are described as clinically diagnosed FTD without explicit specification as behavioral-variant FTD. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) clearly apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a multicenter 18F-FDG PET study that (1) used FDG-PET imaging (I3), (2) included a dedicated FTD group comprised of the ‘frontal variant’ of FTD (bvFTD equivalent) and excluded semantic dementia/PPA (I4), (3) had adequate sample sizes (FTD n=98; controls n=110) meeting the ≥6 requirement (I5), (4) performed voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses after spatial normalization to the Talairach atlas and reported group-level voxelwise patterns comparing FTD to controls (3D-SSP Z maps) satisfying between-group contrast reporting in a defined stereotactic space (I6–I7), and (5) presents whole-brain results in figures and supplemental materials consistent with acceptable reporting (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study uses VBM (I3) and includes patient groups with >=6 participants (FTD n=9; controls n=10) (I5). However it does NOT include a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease sample explicitly (I4 not met). Critically, the neuroimaging results are reported as correlations across all diagnostic groups (a covariate-only VBM analysis) rather than as a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls; therefore no bvFTD-specific group-level whole-brain results are reported (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Because one or more required inclusion criteria for the review (I4, I6, I7) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because, although it uses voxelwise longitudinal morphometry (VBM-style) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes, the imaging results are reported for a combined FTLD group (bvFTD + svPPA) rather than for a bvFTD-only group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxelwise structural MRI/longitudinal VBM-style analysis), I4 (bvFTD participants are included in the sample), I5 (patient and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported for bvFTD alone versus controls; bvFTD was pooled with svPPA), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-only target group). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Because the review requires bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts, this paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria.

This is an original empirical study that uses VBM (FSL-VBM) for whole-brain voxelwise grey matter analyses and reports group-level contrasts for behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) versus healthy controls. The sample includes 7 bvFTD participants and 40 healthy controls (both >6), satisfying sample-size requirements. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (TFCE-corrected maps) with MNI coordinates shown in figures, and bvFTD-specific contrasts are presented (bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups). ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are provided. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study uses FDG-PET and reports voxelwise, whole-brain group contrasts between frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) patients and controls, with adequate sample sizes. However, it does NOT specifically include or report results for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as required. The patient group is labeled as FTLD (heterogeneous umbrella) and the contrasts are reported for FTLD vs controls (not bvFTD specifically). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I6 are not met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (>=6 patients), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not specify bvFTD/Pick’s), I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD group vs controls). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical MRI volumetry study using manual cortical parcellation/ROI volumetry, not a voxelwise whole-brain VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET study required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients, i.e., the behavioral-variant FTD subtype as one of the defined FTLD subtypes) and I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=12, PNFA n=9, SD n=13; controls n=27, all ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is manual ROI volumetry on T1-weighted MRI, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates; results are regional volume comparisons and discriminant analyses), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results).
